evidence.claim: Reuters reporting said the accidental launch raised questions about safety mechanisms and could have endangered passenger flights and civilians.
evidence.title: India says it accidentally fired missile into Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reporting said the accidental launch raised questions about safety mechanisms and could have endangered passenger flights and civilians.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraphs of the Reuters report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced contemporaneous reporting adds independent corroboration to the official admission.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to the same incident as the official statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects the consequences of the Indian state apparatus under Modi's tenure, not a direct ruler order.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes that the missile was unarmed and that the incident was framed as accidental, so it does not by itself show deliberate escalation.

evidence.claim: The article says India’s nuclear release authority remains with civilian authorities and that only the prime minister and designated successors can order nuclear use.
evidence.title: Striking Asymmetries: Nuclear Transitions in Southern Asia
evidence.excerpt: The article says India’s nuclear release authority remains with civilian authorities and that only the prime minister and designated successors can order nuclear use.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Analytical scholarship, not primary law, but it directly summarizes India’s command-and-control arrangement and is dated to the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and directly relevant to the ruler-period authority structure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Civilian command is a real authority attribute of the PM; the passage speaks to what Modi could personally authorize.
contrary_evidence: This is doctrine/structure, not evidence that Modi exercised the authority in 2022 in a risk-reducing way.

evidence.claim: The 2022 amendment bill sought to prohibit financing of WMD-related activity and empower the government to freeze or seize assets tied to such financing.
evidence.title: The Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Amendment Bill, 2022
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 amendment bill sought to prohibit financing of WMD-related activity and empower the government to freeze or seize assets tied to such financing.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary parliamentary/government release describing the enacted policy change in 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to dual-use and proliferation controls.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a government policy decision under Modi’s administration, though not a personal technical action by him.
contrary_evidence: The measure strengthens legal tools but does not prove enforcement success or show that India faced a specific imminent proliferation problem in 2022.
